title: Tolerate memory-churn mutations; gate only checks source integrity
context: Async post-commit auto-capture and gate's own repository-index regeneration mutate memory artifacts (.hunch/**, grounding docs) during a ~25-minute gate run, causing false failures despite source being clean.
decision: Classify paths as memory churn (derived artifacts) or source code. Filter these from all status checks and tolerate HEAD moves if every changed path is churn. Itemize tolerated commits in receipt for auditability.
consequences: Gate can overlap with concurrent memory captures without false failures
Gate's own regeneration of grounding docs doesn't block success
Receipt gains tolerated_memory_commits field for transparency
Status checks now normalize away churn, reducing noise in error reporting
alternatives_rejected: Serialize memory updates by waiting for gate completion (would slow feedback loop)
Ignore churn entirely without tracking (loses auditability of what moved)
Strict file locking on memory paths (complex, fragile, doesn't scale)
Accept any source path changes (defeats entire purpose of release gate)
